note: Every identifier, venue detail and URL here was written from memory without network access and is UNVERIFIED. scripts/review/fetch_papers.py checks that each download is a real PDF; check the bibliographic details before citing them. Set verified to true on an entry once you have checked it.

papers.title: Attention Is All You Need
papers.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 30 (NIPS 2017)

neighbours.title: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate
neighbours.why: Introduced attention on top of a recurrent encoder-decoder; the Transformer keeps the attention and drops the recurrence.

neighbours.title: Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks
neighbours.why: The recurrent sequence-to-sequence baseline the Transformer was built to replace.

neighbours.title: Convolutional Sequence to Sequence Learning
neighbours.why: The competing non-recurrent design from the same months; the Transformer's results tables compare against it.

neighbours.title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
neighbours.why: Took the Transformer encoder into large-scale pre-training, which is how most readers met the architecture.

neighbours.title: Improving Language Understanding by Generative Pre-Training
neighbours.why: The first GPT: the Transformer decoder as a pre-trained language model.

papers.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
papers.venue: IEEE Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR 2016); arXiv December 2015

neighbours.title: Very Deep Convolutional Networks for Large-Scale Image Recognition
neighbours.why: VGG showed depth helps up to about 19 layers; ResNet's starting point is why going deeper stopped helping.

neighbours.title: Highway Networks
neighbours.why: Gated shortcut connections for very deep networks months earlier; ResNet's identity shortcuts are the ungated special case.

neighbours.title: Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training by Reducing Internal Covariate Shift
neighbours.why: ResNet relies on batch normalisation and argues the degradation problem is not vanishing gradients because of it.

neighbours.title: Identity Mappings in Deep Residual Networks
neighbours.why: The authors' own follow-up explaining why clean identity paths matter and moving to pre-activation blocks.

neighbours.title: Residual Networks Behave Like Ensembles of Relatively Shallow Networks
neighbours.why: Challenges the 'very deep' reading: most gradient flows through short paths.

neighbours.title: Research Priorities for Robust and Beneficial Artificial Intelligence
neighbours.why: The broad research agenda that Concrete Problems narrowed into five machine-learning problems.

neighbours.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning from Human Preferences
neighbours.why: A direct attack on the scalable-oversight problem the paper names; the root of RLHF. Also an oracle in eval/spike.

neighbours.title: AI Safety Gridworlds
neighbours.why: Turns several of the paper's problems (side effects, safe exploration, distributional shift) into test environments.

neighbours.title: Risks from Learned Optimization in Advanced Machine Learning Systems
neighbours.why: Adds a failure mode the 2016 taxonomy lacks: inner misalignment. Also an oracle in eval/spike.

neighbours.title: Unsolved Problems in ML Safety
neighbours.why: A deliberate five-years-later update of the agenda, with two of the original authors.

papers.title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models

neighbours.title: Deep Learning Scaling is Predictable, Empirically
neighbours.why: Earlier power-law fits of loss against data and model size across several domains.

neighbours.title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
neighbours.why: GPT-3: the large model whose sizing these laws were used to justify.

neighbours.title: Scaling Laws for Autoregressive Generative Modeling
neighbours.why: Extends the same fits to images, video and mathematics.

neighbours.title: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models
neighbours.why: Chinchilla: revises the compute-optimal split between parameters and tokens, largely because of learning-rate schedule choices in Kaplan et al.

papers.title: The Impact of the Mariel Boatlift on the Miami Labor Market
papers.notes: Sole-authored, although it is often remembered as a co-authored study. The NBER working paper (w3069, 1989) is the likely open copy and may differ slightly from the journal version.

neighbours.title: The Wage Impact of the Marielitos: A Reappraisal
neighbours.why: Reanalyses the boatlift for non-Hispanic men without a high-school diploma and finds large wage declines.

neighbours.title: The Labor Market Effects of a Refugee Wave: Synthetic Control Method Meets the Mariel Boatlift
neighbours.why: Rebuilds the comparison group with synthetic control and finds no significant wage effect, siding with Card.

neighbours.title: The Labor Market Effects of Refugee Waves: Reconciling Conflicting Results
neighbours.why: Argues the Borjas result is driven by a change in the survey's sample composition around 1980.

neighbours.title: Immigrant Inflows, Native Outflows, and the Local Labor Market Impacts of Higher Immigration
neighbours.why: Card's own generalisation from one natural experiment to cross-city variation in immigrant inflows.

papers.title: Minimum Wages and Employment: A Case Study of the Fast-Food Industry in New Jersey and Pennsylvania
papers.notes: The NBER working paper (w4509, 1993) is the likely open copy.

neighbours.title: The Effect of the Minimum Wage on the Fast-Food Industry
neighbours.why: The same survey design applied to Texas fast-food restaurants two years earlier.

neighbours.title: Minimum Wages and Employment: A Case Study of the Fast-Food Industry in New Jersey and Pennsylvania: Comment
neighbours.why: Uses payroll records instead of telephone surveys and finds employment fell in New Jersey.

neighbours.title: Minimum Wages and Employment: A Case Study of the Fast-Food Industry in New Jersey and Pennsylvania: Reply
neighbours.why: The authors' reply using BLS administrative data.

neighbours.title: Minimum Wage Effects Across State Borders: Estimates Using Contiguous Counties
neighbours.why: Generalises the border comparison to every contiguous county pair in the US.

neighbours.title: The Effect of Minimum Wages on Low-Wage Jobs
neighbours.why: A bunching estimator across 138 state minimum-wage changes; the modern version of the question.

papers.title: The Market for "Lemons": Quality Uncertainty and the Market Mechanism
papers.notes: No known stable open-access copy; fetch through a library and drop it in by hand.

neighbours.title: Uncertainty and the Welfare Economics of Medical Care
neighbours.why: Earlier treatment of information asymmetry and non-market institutions in health care.

neighbours.title: Job Market Signaling
neighbours.why: How the informed side can escape the lemons problem by sending a costly signal.

neighbours.title: Equilibrium in Competitive Insurance Markets: An Essay on the Economics of Imperfect Information
neighbours.why: Screening by the uninformed side; insurance markets as the canonical application.

neighbours.title: A Direct Test of the "Lemons" Model: The Market for Used Pickup Trucks
neighbours.why: An early empirical test that finds little evidence of lemons in used trucks.

neighbours.title: Selection in Insurance Markets: Theory and Empirics in Pictures
neighbours.why: A readable modern account of how adverse selection is measured.

papers.title: The China Syndrome: Local Labor Market Effects of Import Competition in the United States

neighbours.title: Factor Immobility and Regional Impacts of Trade Liberalization: Evidence on Poverty from India
neighbours.why: The regional-exposure design (industry mix times national tariff change) that the paper adapts.

neighbours.title: The Surprisingly Swift Decline of US Manufacturing Employment
neighbours.why: Attributes the same decline to China's permanent normal trade relations, using a policy rather than an import measure.

neighbours.title: Import Competition and the Great US Employment Sag of the 2000s
neighbours.why: Adds input-output linkages and puts a national number on jobs lost to Chinese imports.

neighbours.title: The China Shock: Learning from Labor-Market Adjustment to Large Changes in Trade
neighbours.why: The authors' own review of what the China-shock literature found.

neighbours.title: Bartik Instruments: What, When, Why, and How
neighbours.why: Methodological scrutiny of shift-share instruments like the one the paper uses.

papers.title: Does Compulsory School Attendance Affect Schooling and Earnings?
papers.notes: The NBER working paper (w3572, 1990) is the likely open copy.

neighbours.title: Estimating the Returns to Schooling: Some Econometric Problems
neighbours.why: States the ability-bias problem that quarter-of-birth instruments were meant to solve.

neighbours.title: Problems with Instrumental Variables Estimation When the Correlation Between the Instruments and the Endogenous Explanatory Variable is Weak
neighbours.why: Shows that randomly generated quarters of birth reproduce estimates close to the paper's: the weak-instrument critique.

neighbours.title: Instrumental Variables Regression with Weak Instruments
neighbours.why: The econometric theory, and the first-stage F rule of thumb, that came out of the critique.

neighbours.title: The Causal Effect of Education on Earnings
neighbours.why: Places the quarter-of-birth estimates among the other natural-experiment estimates of returns to schooling.

neighbours.title: Season of Birth and Later Outcomes: Old Questions, New Answers
neighbours.why: Mothers' characteristics vary by season of birth, which threatens the exclusion restriction.
